start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:send-my-batches-into-my-list with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_shop on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-shop-postgres-connection\"} and the batches in payloads."
no_lists_because: It names no list of its own: the batches an export wrote carry their own list ids, and the rows go into the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps them.
instructions: 1. Run tool:export-records-as-list-rows first so a payloads folder holds manifest.json and its batch files such as orders-000.json.
2. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.

3. Read manifest.json and each batch file in the manifest's order, and say "Run workflow:send-my-batches-into-my-list" with store and batches as read. Add done (the batches an earlier run already sent) and limits when you have them.
4. The first run proves the send on the example attempts in a throwaway place. Every answer must be the one the intent says, or the run stops and says which.

5. Read what came back: state, batches_done and, if it stopped, the batch that was refused and why. Run it again with the batches_done it gave as done: sent batches are skipped, so a re-run only sends what is left.

worked_examples.title: One batch of two rows is sent into the orders list
worked_examples.ask: Send my prepared bakery orders into my orders list.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The prove step gave the answers the intent says on the example attempts (a PGlite database and a JSON folder gave the same answers), and the store holds no orders yet.
worked_examples.hands_back: state all_batches_sent, batches_done {"orders-000.json": 2}. Run it again with that batches_done as done: it sends nothing.
